why: Lets a shell with more bounces than any shipped type draw an unbounded row. The renderer's instance buffer is sized as shells x MAX_TRAIL_SEGMENTS, so an unclamped count is what would turn a data change into fewer shells getting a trail at all -- and a row too long to count at a glance stops being a count.
killedBy: shell bounce-trail vocabulary (issue #688) clamps to the renderer budget at both ends
